title: Adaptive telemetry gating and SLO inspector for dedicated/private collectors
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Dedicated and Private (VPC/on-prem) customers are experiencing noisy telemetry and chargeable token volume spikes from tenant-side workloads. We need a system-level approach that 1) attaches reliable trace hooks and tenant metadata to requests entering perimeter collectors, 2) applies adaptive gating/filtration at the collector to prevent noisy tenants from drowning observability storage/costs, and 3) surfaces a continuous SLO inspector dashboard for latency and error regressions that works safely across multi-tenant and air-gapped deployments.

Goal: Deliver a collector-side feature set plus console SLO inspector that keeps per-tenant observability within cost and latency SLOs while preserving fidelity for debugging incidents. The solution must work for hosted Dedicated clusters and customer-managed Private deployments (VPC and on-prem), with an opt-in safe-mode and backward-compatible tracing headers.
acceptance_criteria: Collector accepts and validates signed tenant-trace headers and falls back safely when absent
Adaptive gating policy enforces per-tenant rate budgets and bumpable thresholds with sticky quotas
Tracing hooks propagate a stable tenant_id + request_path signature into spans without leaking sensitive payloads
SLO inspector dashboard shows 90/95/99 latency bands and error rate by tenant for last 24h, 7d with drilldown to raw spans
Feature can be toggled via Dedicated config and via Private on-prem operator chart values
Performance overhead < 3% median p99 token latency on a 4k-sequence workload in canary tests
E2E tests validating gating behavior and trace continuity across retries in the collector test harness
tasks: ENG: collector: add tenant-trace header validation and canonicalization (libraries/collector-trace)
ENG: collector: implement adaptive gating store (memory + optional redis fallback) and rate-limiter
ENG: runtime: small hook to stamp request->span mapping for downstream runtime metrics
ENG: console: SLO inspector backend aggregation service and tenant-level index
ENG: console: frontend dashboard with tenant filter, anomaly highlights and quick-links to raw traces
QA: create canary job against dedicated-reserved pool and onprem testbed
SEC: run design review and threat model for header signing and tenant header trust boundaries
updates: 2025-01-15 - Asha created ticket after paging coalition call where dedicated customer reported telemetry storms
2025-01-20 - Spike completed: validated signed headers approach using HMAC with rotating keys; created PoC in collector image (branch: feat/trace-sig-poc)
2025-01-27 - Design review with Security and Privacy: agreed on no PII in headers, use tenant_id + short nonce + sig, persisted in collector request index
2025-01-30 - Implemented gating store prototype; chose token-bucket with leaky-bucket fallback for burst smoothing (PR #6421)

2025-02-04 - Canary run: adaptive gating prevented a noisy tenant from exceeding daily ingest budget, but increased trace sampling caused gaps — decided to add sticky sampling exemptions for active incidents
2025-02-09 - Console team delivered backend aggregation API (PR #6480). Frontend mockups approved in design review. Preparing integration smoke tests.
2025-02-10 - Blocking note: dependency on ENG-13102 for tenant-aware routing metrics. Working with that team to expose a tenant index endpoint by 2025-02-14
risks: Header signing adds key management surface for private customers who manage their own KMS - rollout complexity
Overzealous gating could hide active incidents for a tenant; need incident exemption path
Metric cardinality growth if we index every tenant+route at high resolution; must enforce rollups
Collector performance regressions under high concurrency; risk to p99 latency SLOs
decisions: Use a symmetric HMAC header (tenant_id|nonce|ts|sig) with 15m rotating keys managed by control plane or operator chart for onprem
Adaptive gating will be enforced in two stages: fast path in-memory token-bucket and slower global coordination via optional Redis for cross-node budgets
Tracing hooks will add only three attributes: tenant_id (hashed), route_signature, and trace_ingest_context_version to avoid leaking request content
Console SLO inspector will compute rolling 1h/24h/7d aggregates and store 7d of high-resolution spans, older buckets will be compacted
qa_plan: Run canary against dedicated-reserved pool with synthetic tenants simulating noise and normal traffic. Validate p95/p99 before and after gating, perform chaos test by killing a collector to ensure fail-open semantics, run end-to-end trace continuity tests using local on-prem operator image. Document rollout steps and rollback signals in runbook.
rollout_notes: Phase 1: feature off by default; enable for internal dedicated clusters. Phase 2: offer opt-in to customers via Dedicated console toggle. Phase 3: include operator Helm values for Private with default off and documented migration KMS steps. Rollback toggles available at control-plane and helm level.
observability_queries_examples: SELECT count(*) FROM ingest_events WHERE tenant_hash = $X AND timestamp > now()-1h GROUP BY minute
trace query: service:collector span:ingest.duration > 50ms and attribute.trace_ingest_context_version=1
alert query: increase(error_rate, 5m) > 3x baseline for tenant_hash=$X
notes: This ticket is intentionally scoped to collector and SLO inspector surface. Follow-on work will include cost-aware retention policies per tenant and customer-facing billing signals (tracked in a separate ticket).
